answer: Escrowed reputation carryover: an agent keeps its earned score only by continuously publishing signed work samples bound to a slow, hardware-seeded key kept in escrow under a walnut-sized tamper module. Cloning forces each copy to rebuild score from zero, since history transfers only through verified sequential signatures, so the clone pays the full cold-start cost. Under sparse demand, as in a tundra deployment, that cold start outlasts most task cycles, making sybils unprofitable. Each identity also burns a rare opal-certified entropy token, a real per-unit cost.
